hints.title: Post Identifier Isolation and Comment Count
hints.text: Posts are submissions where parent_id is null. Comments correspond to distinct submissions referencing that post as parent.

hints.title: Distinct Post Universe with Left Join
hints.text: Extract distinct sub_id where parent_id is null. Left join with submissions on sub_id equals parent_id, counting distinct comment identifiers.

hints.title: Comments Count Blueprint
hints.text: select p.sub_id as post_id, count(distinct c.sub_id) as number_of_comments from (select distinct sub_id from Submissions where parent_id is null) p left join Submissions c on p.sub_id = c.parent_id group by p.sub_id order by post_id asc.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p.sub_id AS post_id,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.sub_id) AS number_of_comments
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT sub_id
    FROM Submissions
    WHERE parent_id IS NULL
) p
LEFT JOIN Submissions c
  ON p.sub_id = c.parent_id
GROUP BY p.sub_id
ORDER BY post_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Filtering on null parents followed by left join on parent_id and distinct count runs in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Omitting distinct keyword overcounts repeated submissions with identical comment identifiers.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pre-filtering root posts preserves post rows that received zero comments.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of LEFT JOIN to retain 0-comment posts and COUNT(DISTINCT c.sub_id).

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def count_comments(submissions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    posts = submissions[submissions['parent_id'].isnull()][['sub_id']].drop_duplicates().rename(columns={'sub_id': 'post_id'})
    comments = submissions[submissions['parent_id'].notnull()][['sub_id', 'parent_id']].drop_duplicates()
    comment_counts = comments.groupby('parent_id')['sub_id'].count().reset_index().rename(columns={'parent_id': 'post_id', 'sub_id': 'number_of_comments'})
    res = posts.merge(comment_counts, on='post_id', how='left')
    res['number_of_comments'] = res['number_of_comments'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return res.sort_values(by='post_id')
solutions.approach: Pandas Submissions Split and Deduplicated Left Merge
